Aggregate a panel over time and across individuals

Source: R/aggregate.R
panel_aggregate.Rd

Aggregate a panel over time and across individuals

Usage

panel_aggregate(
  x,
  vars = NULL,
  by = NULL,
  period = NULL,
  fun_time = "mean",
  fun_group = "mean",
  min_n = NULL
)

Arguments

x

A tidy_panel from as_panel().

vars

Numeric columns to summarise; default all numeric columns.

by

Grouping column(s) to aggregate individuals into (e.g. a region); NULL for one overall series. Use ".id" to keep individuals.

period

Coarsen time to "hour", "day", "week", "month", "quarter" or "year", or "all" to collapse time completely (one value per group); NULL keeps the native frequency. Irregular timestamps (kind = "time") must be given a period.

fun_time

Summary applied within each individual when several periods collapse into one (default "mean"; use "sum" for flows).

fun_group

Summary applied across individuals in a group (default "mean"). A name (mean, median, sum, sd, min, max, first, last, n, share, p90, ...) or a function.

min_n

Drop group-periods with fewer than this many individuals (a privacy / noise threshold).

Value

A tibble with .period, the by columns, the vars, and .n (individuals contributing).

Examples

d <- data.frame(who = rep(1:6, each = 4), yr = rep(2001:2004, 6),
                grp = rep(c("x", "y"), each = 12), y = seq_len(24))
p <- as_panel(d, who, yr)
panel_aggregate(p, "y", by = "grp")
#> # A tibble: 8 × 4
#>   .period    grp       y    .n
#>   <date>     <chr> <dbl> <int>
#> 1 2001-01-01 x         5     3
#> 2 2002-01-01 x         6     3
#> 3 2003-01-01 x         7     3
#> 4 2004-01-01 x         8     3
#> 5 2001-01-01 y        17     3
#> 6 2002-01-01 y        18     3
#> 7 2003-01-01 y        19     3
#> 8 2004-01-01 y        20     3
